content: Pyrimethamine, commonly known by the brand name Daraprim, is a medication used in combination with other drugs, such as sulfonamides, to treat severe parasitic infections like toxoplasmosis. This condition can affect the body, brain, or eyes. It is also used to prevent toxoplasmosis in individuals with HIV infection. Pyrimethamine belongs to a class of drugs called antiparasitics. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. To minimize nausea and vomiting, take the medication with food. If vomiting becomes severe or persistent, your doctor may adjust your dose or advise you to stop taking the medication. Your doctor will prescribe folic or folinic acid alongside pyrimethamine to prevent blood-related complications caused by the drug. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. The medication is most effective when its levels in your body are kept constant. Take pyrimethamine and any other prescribed antiparasitic drugs regularly and exactly as directed. The dosage depends on the type of infection, your medical condition, age, and response to treatment. The duration of treatment will vary based on the infection being treated. Your doctor will carefully adjust your dose to treat the infection while minimizing the risk of serious side effects. Do not take more or less of this medication than prescribed. Do not stop taking it before completing the full course, even if you feel better. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite. Serious side effects, such as blood disorders, may occur, especially at higher doses. These risks can be reduced with the use of folic or folinic acid and regular blood tests. Rarely, a severe allergic reaction may occur. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Precautions: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to pyrimethamine or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Folic acid is particularly important during pregnancy. Pyrimethamine passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: Regular laboratory and/or medical tests (such as complete blood count and liver function tests) should be performed while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
